// Positive fixture: every cfg'd construct below ENDS early (a field, a
// variant, a match arm), so each production hit after it MUST be reported.
// Also the lexer's hard cases. Read as TEXT by
// tests/workspace_assumptions_are_enumerated.rs; never compiled.
struct Handles {
    #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]
    stdout_raw_handle: Option<isize>,
    #[cfg(test)]
    test_only: HashMap<String, u8>,
    name: String,
}

fn after_cfg_field() -> &'static str {
    "http://localhost:8000"
}

enum Mode {
    Prod,
    #[cfg(test)]
    Test,
}

fn after_cfg_variant() -> &'static str {
    "http://localhost:3001"
}

fn cfg_match_arm(m: Mode) -> &'static str {
    match m {
        #[cfg(test)]
        Mode::Test => "/home/test-only-arm",
        Mode::Prod => "D:/after/arm",
    }
}

fn after_cfg_match_arm() -> &'static str {
    "C:/after/the/match"
}

fn lexer_raw_string() -> &'static str {
    let _ = r#"a "quoted" // not a comment"#;
    "/home/someone/after-raw"
}

/* outer /* nested */ "http://localhost:8000" still inside the outer comment */
fn lexer_nested_comment() -> &'static str {
    "C:/after/nested"
}

fn lexer_chars() -> (char, char, &'static str) {
    ('\'', '/', "http://127.0.0.1:9875/x")
}

fn lexer_lifetime<'a>(x: &'a str) -> &'a str {
    let _: &'a str = "localhost:6379";
    x
}

#[cfg(windows)]
impl Handles {
    fn windows_method_without_sibling() {}
}

#[cfg(windows)]
mod win_outer {
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        fn inner_test() -> &'static str {
            "http://localhost:8000"
        }
    }
}

fn after_nested_regions() -> u16 {
    9875
}

// Region STACK, both directions. The outer `cfg(windows)` must survive the
// inner `cfg(test)` module: after `tests` closes we are still inside windows,
// so the `taskkill` literal below is NOT reported (os_bound_tooling is
// suppressed under windows) while the machine_path literal beside it IS.
// Flatten the stack to a single region and both verdicts flip.
#[cfg(windows)]
mod win_stack {
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        fn t() -> &'static str {
            "D:/test-only"
        }
    }

    pub fn after_nested_test_mod() -> &'static str {
        let _ = std::process::Command::new("taskkill").arg("/F").status();
        "D:/reported-under-windows"
    }
}

// An FFI declaration inside an already-cfg'd module: the `extern` block, not
// the cfg attribute, is what exempts it from the windows-sibling check —
// a declaration has no body and so can never grow a sibling.
#[cfg(windows)]
mod win_ffi {
    #[link(name = "ntdll")]
    extern "system" {
        fn GetLastErrorShim() -> u32;
    }
}

// `extern "C" fn` is a FN, not an FFI block: its `{` is the fn's own. If it
// armed the FFI scope, that arming would survive to the `impl Console {`
// below, which would then swallow the `Console::` qualification (changing the
// disposition KEY) and exempt `win_only` from the windows-sibling check — so
// the rows here would read `launcher` with no `win_only` at all.
extern "C" fn cb() -> u32 {
    0
}

impl Console {
    pub fn launcher() -> &'static str {
        "powershell.exe"
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    pub fn win_only(&self) {}
}

// A code-generating template whose lines are attribute-shaped. This block
// demonstrates that such a template does NOT swallow what follows — and it
// does not, either way: without the skeleton gate the template's `#[cfg(test)]`
// opens a region that is never ENTERED (the skeleton blanks the template's
// braces) and dies at the `;` ending this `const`, before `after_template` is
// scanned. The gate itself is pinned where it IS observable — a hit on the very
// line that would open the region — by
// `attribute_shaped_lines_inside_string_literals_are_data`.
pub const TEMPLATE: &str = r#"
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    fn t() {}
}
"#;

fn after_template() -> &'static str {
    "http://localhost:9875/health"
}
